Thus, pulmonary hypertension causes secondary right ventricular dysfunction, or car pulmonale. Car pulmonale is manifest by findings of right-axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and chest x-ray with peripheral edema and hepatomegaly (signs of right-sided heart failure). The enlarged right ventricle is associated with a precordial heave on examination and a pronounced S:2, given the increased pressure of the pulmonary system impacting the closure dynamics of the pulmonic valve.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Cardiomyopathy (Choice A) may be dilated, hypertrophic, or restrictive. While the right ventricle in this patient has hypertrophied, this is secondary to pulmonary hypertension rather than a primary disorder of the myocardium. lntracardiac left-to-right shunting (Choice B) is seen in some congenital cardiac defects such as an atrial septal defect or ventricular septal defect. Oxygenated blood from the left side of the heart passes to the right side of the heart, where it then returns to the pulmonary vasculature. If severe and untreated, the increased blood flow through the pulmonary vasculature can trigger pathologic remodeling of the vessel walls, leading to pulmonary hypertension. Right ventricular hypertrophy follows, causing a right-to-left shunt to occur. This phenomenon is called Eisenmenger syndrome. However, in this case, the pulmonary hypertension is secondary to bronchopulmonary dysplasia, not intracardiac left-to-right shunting. Peripheral pulmonary stenosis (Choice C) and pulmonary outlet obstruction (Choice E) are potential causes of pulmonary hypertension and increased right-sided heart pressure. In this case, the patient's history is more consistent with bronchopulmonary dysplasia as a cause of pulmonary hypertension and right-sided heart failure. Educational Objective: Pulmonary hypertension may be secondary to bronchopulmonary dysplasia in neonates. Car pulmonale, or right heart dysfunction, may follow as a result of the inadequacy of the right ventricle to pump against the thickened, remodeled pulmonary vasculature. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A previously healthy 16-year-old girl comes to the physician because of heavy vaginal bleeding for 5 weeks . Menarche was at the age of 12 years . Menses occur at irregular 30- to 45-day intervals . Examination shows no abnormalities except for blood at the cervical os. On day 21 of her menstrual cycle, her serum progesterone concentration is 0.5 ng/ml (follicular N<3; luteal N>3-5) . Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of these findings?
correctExplanation: The first half of the menstrual cycle, the follicular phase, begins with menses and varies in length. During menses, follicle-stimulating and luteinizing hormone (FSH and LH, respectively) concentrations increase and stimulate the developing follicle. The follicle produces estrogen, which leads to the proliferation of the endometrium in preparation for the implantation of a fertilized ovum. As estrogen rises, a surge occurs, which in turn stimulates a surge in LH that causes ovulation. Immediately following ovulation, the luteal phase begins as the corpus luteum forms. The corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain the endometrial lining, which begins the secretory phase of the endometrium. However, if no implantation occurs, the corpus luteum degrades to the corpus albicans, and estrogen and progesterone concentrations decrease, causing menstruation and minor increases in FSH and LH. On day 21 of this patient's cycle, she would be expected to be in the luteal phase of her menstrual cycle, at which time the corpus luteum should be secreting progesterone. As this patient has a lower than normal progesterone concentration, it is unlikely that ovulation has occurred. Anovulatory cycles can lead to heavy menstrual periods, as estrogen is still being secreted by developing follicles to cause endometrial proliferation, but progesterone concentrations are too low to maintain the endometrium.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Gonadal dysgenesis 45,X (Turner syndrome) (Choice B) is a common cause of primary amenorrhea, which is a result of ovarian dysgenesis. Other signs include the absence of secondary sexual characteristics, short stature, cystic hygroma or webbed neck, swelling in the hands/feet, coarctation of the aorta, bicuspid aortic valve, fused kidney, and infertility. This patient has no physical signs to suggest Turner syndrome. Pituitary tumors (Choice C), such as prolactinomas, can cause menstrual irregularities. However, they are more commonly associated with amenorrhea than menorrhagia, and also may present with galactorrhea. A pituitary tumor would be a less common cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in this patient. Sexual abuse (Choice D) can present with abnormal vaginal bleeding caused by genital trauma, such as a cervical or vaginal laceration. This patient had no signs of trauma on physical examination, and trauma would be less likely to cause bleeding for 5 weeks. Von Willebrand disease (Choice E) is an autosomal dominant inherited bleeding disorder caused by a decreased or dysfunctional von Willebrand factor. It typically presents with epistaxis, ecchymoses, or menorrhagia. However, as it is an inherited disorder, it would have likely been apparent with prior menses, rather than occurring within the past 5 weeks only. Educational Objective: Anovulation can lead to abnormal and heavy uterine bleeding. A luteal phase progesterone concentration that is below the cutoff value is indicative of anovulation. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 9-year-old boy with chronic renal failure is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination 2 days after he began enalapril therapy for hypertension . He feels well. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 92/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 130/70 mm Hg. Cardiac examination shows a normal S1 and S2. No murmurs are heard. There is no peripheral edema. Serum studies show: Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's hyperkalemia?

choices.A: Acute progression of chronic renal failure

correctExplanation: Na• (mEq/L) K+ (mEq/L) Cl· (mEq/L) HCO3· (mEq/L) Urea nitrogen (mg/dl) Creatinine (mg/dl) Before Treatment After Treatment 141 136 4.5 5.4 102 100 18 17 55 57 3.1 3 .1 Enalapril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. ACE inhibitors are a first-line treatment for hypertension since they block the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin 11, which has direct vasoconstrictive effects and promotes salt and water retention. Additionally, inhibition of angiotensin production has the secondary effect of suppressing aldosterone production. Aldosterone is responsible for the retention of sodium and excretion of potassium, and its suppression may lead to hyperkalemia. Other important potential side effects of ACE inhibitors include cough and angioedema.
incorrectExplanation: nd D. Acute progression of chronic renal failure {Choice A) would likely be accompanied by an increase in serum creatinine and evidence of fluid retention, such as worsening hypertension and peripheral edema. Decreased glomerular perfusion {Choice B) does not typically occur as a result of treatment with ACE inhibitors. ACE inhibition leads to dilation of efferent arterioles, which may produce a transient decrease in glomerular filtration rate but does not significantly decrease glomerular perfusion unless the patient has underlying renal artery stenosis. Metabolic acidosis {Choice C) is characterized by a decreased serum concentration of bicarbonate and is often accompanied by perturbations in potassium and chloride concentrations. Enalapril does not commonly cause metabolic acidosis. Causes of primary adrenal insufficiency {Choice D) such as Addison disease or congenital adrenal hyperplasia can produce hyperkalemia through the insufficient production of aldosterone. This patient's onset of symptoms shortly after the initiation of therapy with an ACE inhibitor is more suggestive of ACE inhibition as the cause of his hyperkalemia. Educational Objective: Inhibitors of angiotensin-converting enzyme are first-line agents for the treatment of hypertension and have the secondary effect of suppressing the production of aldosterone. Aldosterone is responsible for the retention of sodium and excretion of potassium, and its suppression may lead to hyperkalemia. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

correctExplanation: Na + K+ Urea nitrogen Creatinine Urine RBC RBC casts 129 mEq/L 9 mEq/L 130 mg/dL 10.2 mg/dL >100/hpf occasional Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disorder with a wide range of presentations. Cutaneous manifestations include an erythematous rash over the malar cheeks that spares the nasolabial folds after sun exposure or discoid lesions with hyperpigmented edges and pink, atrophic centers. Painless oral ulcers and nonspecific hair loss may also occur. Fatigue, joint pain, and a fever are also common presenting signs. Lupus nephritis is a complication of SLE and is common in younger women; it can present with hypertension, hematuria, and increased creatinine in the setting of SLE. Laboratory evaluation generally shows a low complement concentration. Lupus nephritis leads to acute kidney injury (AKI) with increased creatinine, which can present with oliguria or anuria. Patients may be asymptomatic or demonstrate symptoms of uremia (eg, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, altered mental status), hyperkalemia (eg, peaked T waves on ECG), and hypervolemia if the AKI is severe. Severe hyperkalemia leads to decreased myocardial excitability resulting in repolarization abnormalities, conduction dysfunction, heart block, and bradycardia. These abnormalities can manifest on an ECG with peaked T waves, PR interval prolongation, loss of P waves, and, if severe, widened QRS complex and bradycardia. Hyperkalemia resulting in ECG changes requires the emergent administration of calcium gluconate or calcium chloride to induce cardiac cell membrane stabilization. Further treatment after calcium may involve insulin and glucose, ~-adrenergic agonists, or bicarbonate to shift potassium into cells, loop diuretics to facilitate the urinary excretion of potassium, and sodium polystyrene sulfonate to promote binding of potassium within the lumen of the gut. For severe or refractory cases, dialysis may be necessary.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Bolus of methylprednisolone (Choice A) may be used in the treatment of severe manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus, such as lupus nephritis in this patient. However, immediate management of the patient's hyperkalemia with calcium chloride would be the next appropriate step in management. Intravenous administration of 0.9% sodium chloride (Choice C) is less appropriate than stabilization of the cardiac membrane with calcium. This patient does have mild hyponatremia, likely caused by renal failure and volume overload. Immediate management should be focused on hyperkalemia, which can be complicated by bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Plasmapheresis (Choice D) would not be the next step in management for this patient as it does not significantly affect the potassium concentration. Plasmapheresis can be used for the removal of circulating immune complexes or pathogenic antibodies, such as in thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Patients with severe hyperkalemia may require hemodialysis (Choice E), however, the first step requires the administration of calcium chloride to emergently stabilize the myocardial membrane prior to attempting to lower potassium concentrations with medications and/or dialysis, if refractory. Educational Objective: Acute renal failure can lead to hypertension and hyperkalemia. Severe hyperkalemia resulting in ECG changes requires the emergent administration of calcium gluconate or calcium chloride to induce cardiac cell membrane stabilization. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A previously healthy 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after falling against the crossbar of his bicycle in a straddle position . He has not voided since that time. He appears to be in severe pain. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 120/min, respirations are 25/min , and blood pressure is 105/75 mm Hg. Examination shows a large perinea! hematoma and blood at the urethral meatus . No other abnormalities are noted. X-ray of the pelvis shows no abnormalities . Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
correctExplanation: A straddle injury resulting in a large perinea! hematoma and blood at the urethral meatus raises concern for a urethral injury. Urethral injuries are characterized by difficulty voiding, blood at the urethral meatus, perinea! ecchymosis, and may be associated with a pelvic fracture. Straddle injuries can cause trauma to the anterior urethra, while pelvic fractures may injure the posterior urethra. Anterior urethral injuries are evaluated by a retrograde urethrography, which involves the injection of contrast into the urethra to evaluate for the extravasation of contrast, indicating urethral discontinuity. Depending on the location and severity of urethral injury, patients may require surgical repair or the placement of a urethral catheter to help promote healing and prevent complications of urinary extravasation, infection, urethrocutaneous fistula, or urethral stricture.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Renal ultrasonography (Choice A) would be limited in the evaluation of traumatic injuries, and is typically performed for the evaluation of hydronephrosis, vesicoureteral reflux, and congenital urinary tract abnormalities. CT scan of the abdomen (Choice C) would be helpful in diagnosing other traumatic injuries such as liver or splenic lacerations, duodenal hematoma, bowel perforation, or retroperitoneal hematoma. However, for a suspected urethral injury, retrograde urethrography would be the initial imaging of choice. Intravenous pyelography (Choice D) involves the intravenous injection of radiopaque contrast to subsequently visualize the kidney collecting system, ureters, and bladder under fluoroscopy. This allows for the investigation of suspected urinary tract anatomic abnormalities, malignancies, and strictures. Insertion of a urinary catheter (Choice E) would be contraindicated as the first step in management in a patient with blood at the urethral meatus, portending a likely urethral injury. It may cause further trauma and injury to the urethra and internal pelvic structures without the injury first being delineated on retrograde urethrography. Educational Objective: Urethral injuries can occur from straddle injuries (anterior urethra) or pelvic fractures (posterior urethra). Retrograde urethrography permits evaluation of the urethra as a source of hematuria. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 7-year-old Hispanic girl with a 1-year history of acute lymphocytic leukemia is brought to the physician for a routine examination 6 weeks after starting treatment with two new chemotherapeutic medications . She has had decreased appetite , nausea , and increasing hair loss since starting treatment. She was in remission until 2 months ago . The child's parents state that there is an herbal remedy in Mexico that is believed to be a cure for their daughter's condition with few side effects. They ask for the physician's help in obtaining the herbal remedy so they can discontinue their daughter's current medications . Which of the following is the most appropriate response to the parents' request?

choices.A: Advise them to continue her medications while investigating the information further
choices.C: Dismiss the idea because it is unproven
choices.D: Offer to add the herbal remedy to the patient's current regimen
choices.E: Offer to transfer the daughter to a hospital in Mexico
choices.G: Recommend they find another physician if alternative medications are used

correctExplanation: When families inquire about naturopathic (alternative) treatments for patients being treated for life-threatening diseases, physicians should advise the family to continue the evidence-based treatment until the physician can further investigate the naturopathic treatment. Though patient and family autonomy are important factors in many medical situations (eg, adult patients with decisional capacity may opt to forgo an evidence-based treatment in favor of a naturopathic treatment), physicians should not withhold life-saving treatments from patients who lack decisional capacity, such as children. The physician should, however, research the herbal remedy and discuss the risks and benefits of all treatment options with the family to address knowledge gaps and collaboratively develop a treatment plan that aligns with their values. If the herbal remedy will not interact with the chemotherapeutic regimen or harm the patient, the remedy may be incorporated into a treatment regimen; however, it should not take the place of medications with known efficacy. If the family maintains that they want to discontinue the life-saving treatment, and the physician believes that this would not be in the child's best interest, the physician may seek legal permission to proceed without parental consent.
incorrectExplanation: nd G. Contacting child protective services (Choice B) or referring the parents for psychiatric assessment (Choice F) imply that the parents may be unable to appropriately care for the patient. In reality, their suggestion to use an herbal remedy may be culturally appropriate and does not likely indicate psychiatric pathology or danger to the patient. Though the physician may ultimately dismiss the idea because it is unproven (Choice C) or offer to add the herbal remedy to the patient's current regimen (Choice D), the physician most likely does not possess sufficient information to make either of these decisions. The physician should first research the naturopathic option. Offering to transfer the daughter to a hospital in Mexico (Choice E) or recommending the parents find another physician if alternative medications are used (Choice G) may decrease the patient's access to life-saving, evidence-based treatment. Physicians should instead discuss the risks and benefits of the treatment options and collaborate with the family to develop a treatment plan. Educational Objective: Physicians should deliver life-saving treatments to patients who lack decisional capacity, such as children. When families inquire about discontinuing evidence-based treatment in favor of naturopathic treatment, physicians should advise the family to continue the evidence-based treatment until the physician can further investigate the naturopathic treatment. After researching the naturopathic treatment, the physician can collaborate with the family to develop a treatment plan that aligns with their values and is in the patient's best interest. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 6-year-old girl with nephrotic syndrome is brought to the physician because of a 2-day history of fever, abdominal swelling , and loose stools. Her temperature is 39.4 °C (103°F). Abdominal examination shows distention , diffuse tenderness , and generalized rebound tenderness in all quadrants . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
correctExplanation: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) is characterized by the bacterial infection of ascitic fluid in the absence of an obvious source of infection (eg, bowel perforation). Patients with underlying conditions that predispose to the formation of ascitic fluid, such as nephrotic syndrome or cirrhosis, are at an increased risk for SBP. SBP may be caused by a variety of bacteria, commonly Escherichia coli and Klebsiel/a species. Patients present with fever, diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, peritoneal signs (eg, rebound tenderness), and leukocytosis. Diagnosis is confirmed with paracentesis demonstrating bacterial growth on cultures or the presence of >250 neutrophils/µL. SBP may rapidly progress to sepsis. Treatment includes supportive care and intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Celiac disease (Choice A), or gluten-sensitive enteropathy, presents with diarrhea and malabsorption caused by gliadin hypersensitivity. It presents with diarrhea but does not present with fever or rebound tenderness. Congenital megacolon (Hirschsprung disease) (Choice B) results from dysmotility caused by abnormal migration of colonic neural crest cells during development. It may present with fever and sepsis as a result of toxic megacolon but is not associated with nephrotic syndrome. Inflammatory bowel disease (Choice C) presents with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea. It is less likely in this patient with a known history of nephrotic syndrome. lntussusception (Choice D) is the telescoping of a segment of bowel into an adjacent segment. It presents with abdominal pain and bloody stool. It does not present with fever unless the affected segment of bowel becomes necrotic. It commonly results secondary to a lead point (eg, Meckel diverticulum, lymphadenopathy) but is not associated with nephrotic syndrome. Necrotizing enterocolitis (Choice E) occurs in premature neonates and is characterized by necrosis of immature bowel. It does not commonly occur in toddlers or children. Educational Objective: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is characterized by the bacterial infection of ascitic fluid in the absence of an obvious source of infection and is a significant cause of mortality in patients with nephrotic syndrome and cirrhosis. Diagnosis is confirmed with paracentesis demonstrating bacterial growth on cultures or the presence of >250 neutrophils/µL. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 3-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother, who is concerned that her daughter might have been abused . The mother states that her daughter has been touching her genital area since she began attending day care 6 weeks ago. The mother says, "I've heard about bad things happening to kids in day care." The patient is a picky eater and is occasionally defiant. She has had intermittent nighttime awakening . She interacts well with other children but sometimes does not want to share her toys. She separates from her mother after initial hesitation when dropped off at the preschool. Her teacher reports no behavior problems . Today, the patient appears mildly anxious . Physical examination shows no abnormalities . Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.A: Reassure the mother that this is normal behavio~
choices.B: Interview the patient for suspected sexual abuse
choices.E: Schedule an appointment with child protective services

correctExplanation: This patient's social development is normative. Starting at age 2 years, toddlers become more curious about their genitalia and associated sensations, along with gender differences. Normative sexual behavior of toddlers includes solitary behaviors such as touching their own genitals along with social behaviors such as looking at another person's genitals. Sexual behaviors that are concerning for sexual abuse (or violence or neglect in the home) include imitations of specific sexual acts, coercive sexual behavior, and excessive preoccupation with sexual behavior. Toddlers typically demonstrate occasional defiance, and cooperative play is not expected to develop until age 4 years, so this child's inclination not to share her toys is typical. Nighttime awakenings, picky eating, and anxiety about physician appointments are also typical for toddlers.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Sexual abuse (Choice B) may lead to sexual behavior problems. Physicians are mandated to investigate and report suspected abuse to child protective services (Choice E). Problem behaviors include imitating sexual acts along with coercive sexual behavior or excessive preoccupation with sexual behavior. Parent management training (Choice C) assists parents in managing excessive oppositional behavior by modeling parent-child interactions. This modality is utilized in oppositional defiant disorder and conduct disorder rather than normative oppositional behavior in toddlers. Recommending individual psychotherapy (Choice D) would be inappropriate in this patient demonstrating normative social behaviors. Educational Objective: Normative sexual behavior of toddlers includes solitary behaviors such as touching their own genitals along with social behaviors such as looking at another person's genitals. Sexual behaviors that are concerning for sexual abuse include imitations of sexual acts, coercive sexual behavior, and excessive preoccupation with sexual behavior. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous
